question: Hill Area Development Programmes were initiated during the ______________ FiveYear Plan covering 15 districts.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fifth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hill Area Development Programme (HADP) was initiated during the Fifth Five-Year Plan in India.
 
• The program aimed at the development of hilly regions and covered 15 districts initially.
 
• The primary objective was to ensure the socio-economic development of these regions which are generally less developed compared to plains.
 
• Special emphasis was placed on improving infrastructure, agriculture, forestry, and human resource development in these areas.
 
• The program recognized the unique geographical and environmental challenges faced by hill areas and aimed to address them through targeted interventions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans in India**

 
 
• The Five-Year Plans were centralized and integrated national economic programs.
 
• They were developed and executed by the Planning Commission of India, which was established in 1950.
 
• The plans aimed to boost the economy through various sector-specific schemes and policies.
 
• Each plan focused on different sectors like agriculture, industry, services, and social development.
 
 
 
• **Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-1979)**
 
 
• This plan focused on poverty alleviation and self-reliance as the main objectives.
 
• It emphasized employment generation and the development of infrastructure.
 
• It also focused on agricultural growth and improving the living standards of the rural population.
 
 
 
• **Hill Area Development**
 
 
• Hill areas often face issues like soil erosion, deforestation, and inadequate infrastructure.
 
• Development programs aim to address these issues through sustainable practices.
 
• Efforts include promoting terrace farming, reforestation, and developing road connectivity.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development**
 
 
• Sustainable development in hill areas focuses on balancing economic growth with environmental conservation.
 
• It involves using resources in a way that meets current needs without compromising future generations.
 
• Key practices include eco-friendly tourism, organic farming, and renewable energy projects.
